Jimmy Kimmel called out President Donald Trump for constantly cooking up ways to profit off his presidency.

“After the big loss for Republicans, Trump is making lemonade,” Kimmel said. “He’s once again milking the MAGA faithful with some hot new merch.”

After Republicans were trounced by Democrats in last week’s midterm elections, Trump said he would become “Mr. Veto.” He placed a red cap with the word “VETO” across it on his desk in the Oval Office ― then immediately started selling those caps in his online store for $55 a pop.

That led Kimmel to a theory.

“He creates new hats to remind him of what he’s supposed to do,” he said. “If he forgets to veto something, he looks in the mirror, he’s like, ‘Oh yeah.’ And then he vetoes.”

Kimmel snarked that the cap was designed to help an aging president remember things ― then showed off a different red cap with the word “WIPE!” written across it.

But the president’s $55 caps are nothing compared to how much he’s earning off his Truth Social website, where subscribers can pay up to $100,000 a month to see his posts in advance, which critics have said could help people trade stocks by getting information about companies from the president before the general public.

“Remember when Trump accused Biden of selling access?” Kimmel asked. “He is literally selling access.”

Kimmel was stunned that this isn’t a bigger story.

“He has people paying him a million dollars a year for information and we barely hear a thing about it,” he said.
